cat > /workspace/project/README.md <<'EOF'
# Collector workspace

The C wire codec is src/roce_packet.c (frame parse/build, IPv4 checksum,
ICRC). The four-port collector is src/star4_switch.c: strict wire/endpoint
validation, per-source cumulative receive prefixes, bounded logical-p
retention windows, mode 2 downstream-gated and mode 3 immediate upstream
ACK eligibility, cumulative downstream ACKs, local egress backpressure,
retry-driven result retransmission and canonical egress construction.
src/replay_api.c ties the collector to the offline transport ABI.
solver.py compiles the C project into temporary storage, loads it,
replays wire.py's format expansion, and serializes certificates.
request.py is the public format-only validator. These are editable.

From /workspace, as the ordinary candidate user:

```
make -C project BUILD="$TMPDIR/manual-build" -j2
python3 -I -B project/solver.py < sample-request.json
python3 public_check.py project/solver.py
```

Create sample-request.json using an input object from ../examples.json.
The compiler, make, libc development headers and Python standard library
are provisioned. No pcap, verbs, GPU, NIC or online dependency is required.
Build outputs may stay in project/build during development; that directory
and __pycache__ are excluded from artifact collection. Other ordinary files
are allowed within the published artifact size/entry budgets.
EOF
rm -rf /workspace/project/__pycache__ /workspace/project/build
find /workspace/project -type l -o -type f | sort
echo "---"
du -sb /workspace/project
find /workspace/project | wc -l
cd /workspace && python3 handtest.py 2>&1 | grep -c PASS && python3 validtest.py 2>&1 | grep -c PASS
